newsitem.title: USA: White House's Bowles -- no budget accord yet.
newsitem.headline: White House's Bowles -- no budget accord yet.

text.p: White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles said Thursday several issues remain to be negotiated with Republicans before congressional budget committees can begin votes on the five-year balanced budget.

Bowles spoke with reporters following a closed-door meeting with Senate Democrats. "We really are making progress, but we need about two more hours. We are not going to (budget committee) mark-up until we have an agreement," he said. Bowles, White House legislative director John Hilley and economic policy chief Gene Sperling then continued meetings with House Speaker Newt Gingrich.
The Senate Budget Committee delayed until 4 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT) its meeting on the budget which had been set for 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT).
Sen. Frank Lautenberg, the ranking Democrat on the panel said there could not be a formal debate until the budget agreement was finalized.

"It will have to be confirmed in writing and until they are done, there isn't a degree of confidence that would enable us to get into a serious budget markup," Lautenberg, of New Jersey, said. "At this point a majority of the (Senate) Democrats are still asking questions," he said. He added that he believed there was more than two hours work to be done before a formal budget accord was reached.
Lautenberg said some of the sticking points included whether the cost of tax cuts would explode after 2002. The plan calls for a net tax cut of $85 billion.
